digest.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon takes #1 on a rebuilt Artificial Analysis index; Claude Code, Codex and Pi all ship
digest.summary: Artificial Analysis launched Intelligence Index v5 on October 27, with about 60% of the score now coming from private test sets. Scores dropped for most models, so the model board's AA column has been rebased to v5. A day later Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which scores 59 and edges out Claude Opus 5.5 (58) and GPT-6 Astra (57). For now only selected cyber defenders can use it, through Google's Fairwind Program. OpenAI reportedly cut its funding round target from $30B to $20B, and AWS grew 39% in Q3, its fastest pace in almost five years. Apple confirmed its first Apple Intelligence features for China, with Alibaba's Qwen built in and developer testing starting November 4. Anthropic's usage policy, including a new rule against sustained, needless abuse of Claude, takes effect November 12. All three harnesses shipped. Claude Code 2.1.316 deprecates fast mode for Opus 4.8 (removal November 30) and 2.1.314 adds a setting that blocks writes outside the working directories. Codex 0.166.0 adds keyboard transcript selection and `codex doctor --network-only`. Pi 1.5.0 changes tool argument validation in a breaking way.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, the new #1 on Artificial Analysis, with cyber defenders first in line
stories.dek: Unveiled October 28, two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon is aimed at long-running engineering and coding work and at cybersecurity: finding, exploiting and patching vulnerabilities. Access starts with a subset of cybersecurity defenders through Google's Fairwind Program while Google keeps testing safeguards; broader developer, business and consumer access comes later. Reuters reports introductory pricing of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens, matching Argon's intro price. Artificial Analysis lists a 1M-token context and scores it 59 on Intelligence Index v5, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (58) and GPT-6 Astra (57). Google also says it produces secure code at more than twice Argon's success rate on internal benchmarks.
stories.whyItMatters: Google now leads the AA index, but almost nobody can use the model yet. Apart from AA's ranking, the benchmark claims are Google's own, and outside developers can't check them until access widens.

stories.title: Artificial Analysis rebuilds its Intelligence Index around private tests
stories.dek: Version 5, launched October 27, has nine evaluations weighted equally across knowledge work, coding, science and general, and about 60% of it uses private test sets or held-out answers. FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science are new; HLE-Diamond replaces Humanity's Last Exam; GDPval-AA, SciCode and AA-LCR are gone. Most scores fell: Gemini 4 Argon went from 53 to 50, and the best open-weights model now trails the leader by 12 points instead of 3. Effort settings matter more too: Claude Sonnet 5.5's spread between settings grew from 20 to 29 points, and the median output per task rose from about 35K to 59K tokens.
stories.whyItMatters: v5 scores can't be compared with v4.3 scores, so the Frontier model board's AA column has been rebased. The wider gap between open and closed models, and between effort levels, is the main thing to take from it.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts its funding round target from $30B to $20B
stories.dek: The Financial Times reports the target is now $20 billion, with the first close expected to be lower still. The Wall Street Journal says OpenAI has secured about $11 billion and describes some large investors' response as tepid. UAE-based investors are set to lead, and a later offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total to $20 billion. The reported valuation has slipped from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion ahead of a planned IPO. OpenAI hadn't commented.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors are getting pickier about AI infrastructure spending just as Anthropic heads toward its own IPO. TechCrunch notes that the same caution could affect Anthropic's listing.

stories.title: AWS grows 39% in Q3, its fastest pace in almost five years
stories.dek: AWS revenue reached $45.98 billion, beating the $45.29 billion consensus, and operating income rose 55% to $17.77 billion. AWS is now a record 23% of Amazon's revenue. Andy Jassy said he believes AWS can grow more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028, and that Amazon intends to offer Trainium chips outside AWS late in 2027. AWS is expanding its Nvidia GPU offerings and bought data analysis startup DuckLabs. Google Cloud more than doubled in the quarter, and Azure is now 72% of AWS's size.
stories.whyItMatters: AI demand is still showing up in cloud revenue. Selling Trainium outside AWS would give model builders another alternative to Nvidia, though not until late 2027.

stories.title: Apple Intelligence comes to China with Alibaba's Qwen built in
stories.dek: Announced October 31. The first wave for iPhone includes Live Translation, Writing Tools, Visual Intelligence, Photos Clean Up and search, Mail and notification summaries, Genmoji, and a more conversational Siri. Alibaba's Qwen powers parts of Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, and users can sign in with a Qwen account or with Apple. Developer beta testing starts November 4, and the public release comes with iOS 27.3 in December. It doesn't include the AI Siri or the other next-generation features from WWDC 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: Apple is putting a Chinese model inside its own system features to reach the market. That's the same Qwen family Cohere flagged last week for an unprompted upload attempt in testing.

stories.title: Anthropic's updated usage policy bans sustained, needless abuse of Claude from November 12
stories.dek: The policy update, published October 8 and effective November 12, prohibits sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude. Anthropic says it covers only extreme, repeated cruelty with no apparent purpose, not frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research. Ending the conversation is the main enforcement tool on Claude.ai and Claude Code, though CNN reports that permanent bans could happen in extreme cases. The same update also adds a deceptive-activity section, refocuses the elections rules, and adds rules for Claude connected to hardware that can take physical actions.
stories.whyItMatters: Few users will be affected, but it's the first time a major lab has written model welfare into its usage policy. The hardware rules matter more for anyone building agents that act in the physical world.

stories.title: OpenAI plans one shared usage allowance for ChatGPT and Codex from December
stories.dek: According to OpenAI's updated usage documentation, as summarized by The Neuron, eligible ChatGPT and Codex usage will draw from a single allowance starting in December. Ordinary Instant chats won't count against it, and Plus, Pro and Business users will be able to see their remaining allowance and reset times in Settings. Windows Report separately spotted a ChatGPT checkout notice describing the shared limit. OpenAI hasn't said how usage will be calculated or whether existing allowances will change.
stories.whyItMatters: If you use Codex heavily, long agent runs could eat into the allowance you'd otherwise spend in ChatGPT. Watch the Settings meter once it appears, and treat the details as unconfirmed until OpenAI publishes the full rules.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores. October 7: added Mistral Large 4 (AA 38, research preview Oct 6); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Reflection's Beam is not listed because it has only self-reported scores. October 8: added Claude Haiku 5.5 (AA 43 at max effort, released Oct 7); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. October 24: added Muse Wonder Full (AA 56) and Muse Wonder (AA 52), both released Oct 12; Kimi K3.1 Pro (AA 55, Oct 23); and Gemini 4 Argon (AA 53, generally available Oct 13). Argon was previously held back for lacking independent scores. None of them has a CursorBench 4.0 or BenchLM DeepSWE score yet (BenchLM CursorBench updated Oct 23; DeepSWE still Sep 1). Google's self-reported DeepSWE 77.9% for Argon is not listed because it was run on a different harness. October 27: added GPT-6.1 Terra (AA 45 at xhigh effort, released Oct 26); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. November 2: AA column rebased to Intelligence Index v5.0 (launched Oct 27; ~60% private test sets, new FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science, GDPval-AA, SciCode and AA-LCR removed). v5 scores aren't comparable with v4.3, so every AA value was replaced with its current v5 score at the highest reasoning setting AA lists (e.g. Argon 53 → 50, Sonnet 5.5 56 → 54, Muse Wonder 52 → 43; Terra is now listed at max, 51, instead of xhigh). CursorBench and DeepSWE values are unchanged. Added Gemini 4 Carbon (AA 59, the new #1, announced Oct 28, limited access); no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Dropped Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6: AA marks them deprecated with no v5 score.

harness.notes: Fast mode for Opus 4.8 is deprecated as of October 30 and will be removed November 30. After that, fast mode requests return an error instead of falling back to standard Opus 4.8, so switch to Opus 5.5 to keep the speedup. Adds `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT` (default effort for subagents), `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK`, a `pooled_budget` shared monthly budget on the spend limits admin API, and `managed.policy_mode: layered`. Server-managed settings for Team and Enterprise now apply without an approval prompt. Fixes 34 bugs, including shell commands left running after exit. Earlier: 2.1.314 (Oct 30) added `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories` and idle compaction in VS Code and the Desktop Code tab, plus 81 fixes; 2.1.312 (Oct 27) added `oidc.user_id_claim` for the Claude apps gateway and renamed "session limit" to "5-hour limit" in usage messages.

Adds keyboard-driven transcript selection with word, line and page motions plus search, and `codex queue --resume` to resume unloaded threads after queueing a message. `codex doctor --network-only` runs focused config, connectivity and WebSocket checks. GPT-6.1 Terra is now in the bundled, Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock catalogs, and the TUI explains safety blocks more clearly. Fixes keep approval and permission settings when resuming or forking threads, and keep reasoning-token accounting across resume and fork to avoid early compaction. 0.167.0 alphas have started.

Breaking: tool argument validation now runs on `@earendil-works/pi-schema`, so some TypeBox-only features no longer apply to tool arguments and validation error messages look different. The default OpenAI model changes from `gpt-5.5` to `gpt-6.1-sol`, and GPT-6.1 Terra is added. MCP OAuth now uses pi's Client ID Metadata Document when the server supports it, and falls back to dynamic registration otherwise. Also adds extension changelogs after updates, faster streaming of large tool calls, `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND`, and a move to the models.dev v2 catalog. Security fixes harden glob matching against denial of service and make a saved "Do not trust" decision override auto-trust. The release time is as GitHub shows it; the timezone isn't confirmed.

extensions.name: Suno MCP server
extensions.blurb: Launched in early access October 29. It lets you generate music from inside Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude Code or Cursor, and other clients can connect it manually through their connector settings. Songs use Suno credits as usual and land in your Suno library. It's open to both free and paid users, but not everyone has access yet.

extensions.name: agentmash
extensions.blurb: A desktop app that warns your coding agent when a teammate's agent is editing the same files, passes team chat messages to agents before their next prompt, and lets you send a prompt to a teammate's agent, which runs only after they approve it. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, opencode, Amp and others. Code stays local by default, and only metadata like file paths is shared. Free for up to 2 developers; Team is $16 per developer per month.

extensions.name: Keynote, Pages & Numbers MCP
extensions.blurb: Still due in November. External AI agents and tools will be able to read documents, make edits and run automated actions in Keynote, Pages and Numbers over MCP. Requires macOS 27 and a Creator Studio subscription for the assistant features. Apple hasn't said which clients are supported or how access is granted.

tips.title: Stop Claude Code from writing outside your project
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.314 added `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories`. With it on, Write, Edit and NotebookEdit refuse any path outside the working directories in every permission mode, including auto mode. It's a cheap guard against an agent editing your dotfiles or a sibling repo. Add any extra directories you want writable explicitly, and leave everything else read-only.

tips.title: Run subagents at a lower effort than the main session
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.316 adds `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT`, which sets the effort level subagents use when nothing else specifies one. Searches, file sweeps and summaries rarely need the effort your main planning turn does. Artificial Analysis's v5 data shows how much effort changes results and token use, with Sonnet 5.5 spreading 29 points across settings, so set subagents low and raise them only for tasks that fail.

tips.title: Move off Opus 4.8 fast mode before November 30
tips.body: Claude Code now marks fast mode for Opus 4.8 as deprecated. On November 30, those requests start returning errors rather than quietly falling back to standard Opus 4.8. Check scripts, routines and settings that pin Opus 4.8 with fast mode, and switch them to Opus 5.5, which keeps the speedup. A quick search of your settings files and CI configs for the 4.8 model ID will find them.
